scenes.headline: How DART makes SAM3 detect many classes
scenes.sub: One backbone pass shared by every class, and no retraining
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Snapdragon! SAM3 finds anything you name, one name at a time. DART makes it detect many classes at once, with no retraining.

scenes.text: SAM3's expensive backbone never sees the text prompt. So run it once per image, and batch only the part that depends on the class.
scenes.say: The insight: SAM3's big backbone never looks at the prompt. So run it once per image, and batch only what depends on the class.

steps.say: A frame goes through the ViT-H backbone once. Four hundred thirty-nine million parameters, and none of them ever see the prompt.
Class names come from a text cache, encoded once. The encoder-decoder runs batched across every class, on the same cached features.
A new scoring head scores all two hundred queries against every class in one matrix multiply. Its weights are copied from SAM3, not learned.
The mask head is dropped, and non-max suppression turns the scores into boxes.

scenes.title: From 336 to 60 milliseconds
scenes.say: Then the speedups, at three classes.

items.say: Naive SAM3 takes three hundred thirty-six milliseconds a frame. Sharing the backbone: one hundred sixty-two.
Batching the decoder and dropping masks: one hundred twelve.
Fused half-precision attention broke the backbone, so it's exported as explicit steps that stay accurate: seventy-eight.
Then the next frame's backbone overlaps this frame's decoder: sixty milliseconds, with no training anywhere.

scenes.label: per image for all 80 COCO classes, the setup behind 55.8 AP
scenes.note: the 15.8 FPS headline is the 4-class row
scenes.say: One caution: fifty-five point eight AP covers all eighty COCO classes, but fifteen point eight frames a second is four. At eighty, the repo times two hundred twenty-five milliseconds.

scenes.text: Find the part of a model that never sees the prompt, and pay for it once.

recap: The backbone never sees the prompt: run it once
The scoring head copies SAM3's weights, batched over classes
Speed depends on class count; read it first
scenes.say: To recap: one prompt-blind backbone pass, a batched decoder, no new weights. And check the class count first.
